2609.31736.title: LukeNet: A lightweight CNN integrated with an XAI model for Smart acute lymphoblastic leukemia detection and management
2609.31736.paper_summary: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) patients require early, accurate detection to enable timely treatment and effective patient management. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is well-suited for creating an end-to-end enabling environment for ALL detection and classification. However, most CNN-based ALL detection systems are theoretical and unsuitable for deployment on edge devices due to high computational demands. The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)-enabled devices offer an opportunity to monitor ALL patients in real time. Wearables that track temperature, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and activity can deliver critical data to support timely clinical intervention and improve patient outcomes. In smart IoMT environments, a lightweight CNN is essential because connected devices often operate under limited computational power, memory, and latency constraints. To address this need, this study proposes LukeNet, a lightweight CNN integrated with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) for an IoMT-based SMART Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Detection and Management System. Trained on three (3) ALL datasets and five-fold cross-validation, LukeNet achieved an impressive 99% model accuracy as well as 99% unseen test accuracy, which is higher than six state-of-the-art (SOTA) CNNs, such as DenseNet121, MobileNet, ResNet50, InceptionV3, Xception, and VGG16, as well as transfer learning models. Furthermore, LukeNet was compared with two ensemble models. In addition, explainable AI methods are integrated to highlight relevant regions in microscopic images. The novelty of this study lies in the architecture of LukeNet, which balances model depth and computational efficiency by using depthwise separable convolutions, mitigates the risk of gradient loss in deeper layers, and provides strong global and local feature extraction capabilities.
2609.31736.paper_summary_zh: 急性淋巴母細胞白血病（ALL）患者需要及早、準確的檢測，以便及時治療和有效管理患者。卷積神經網絡（CNN）非常適合為ALL的檢測和分類創建端到端的支持環境。然而，大多數基於CNN的ALL檢測系統都是理論性的，並不適合在邊緣設備上部署，因為它們對計算能力的需求很高。互聯網醫療事物（IoMT）啟用的設備提供了實時監測ALL患者的機會。可以追蹤體溫、心率、氧飽和度和活動的可穿戴設備能夠提供關鍵數據，以支持及時的臨床干預並改善患者結果。在智能IoMT環境中，輕量級CNN是必不可少的，因為連接的設備通常在有限的計算能力、內存和延遲限制下運行。為了滿足這一需求，本研究提出了LukeNet，一種輕量級CNN，集成了解釋性人工智能（XAI），用於基於IoMT的智能急性淋巴母細胞白血病檢測和管理系統。在三個（3）ALL數據集上進行訓練並進行五次交叉驗證，LukeNet達到了驚人的99%模型準確率以及99%未見測試準確率，這高於六個最先進的（SOTA）CNN，如DenseNet121、MobileNet、ResNet50、InceptionV3、Xception和VGG16，以及遷移學習模型。此外，LukeNet還與兩個集成模型進行了比較。此外，集成了解釋性AI方法，以突出顯微圖像中的相關區域。本研究的創新之處在於LukeNet的架構，它通過使用深度可分離卷積來平衡模型深度和計算效率，減少了深層中的梯度損失風險，並提供了強大的全局和局部特徵提取能力。
